item.title: Solanke scores in added time as 10-man Spurs draw with Man Utd
item.description: Dominic Solanke scores in stoppage time to salvage a point for 10-man Tottenham as they snatch a draw against Manchester United in a feisty encounter at Old Trafford.

item.title: Henderson scores twice as five-star Chelsea thrash Bournemouth
item.description: Jordan Henderson has a home debut to remember as he scores twice for Chelsea as his side thrash Bournemouth 5-1 at Stamford Bridge, leaving the away side still searching for their first Premier League win this season.

item.title: Brilliant Guimaraes goal helps Arsenal fight back to beat Leeds
item.description: A brilliant goal from Bruno Guimaraes helps Arsenal come from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates, as the champions get back to winning ways in the Premier League.

item.title: Struijk sees red but Brighton march on with win against Sunderland
item.description: Brighton maintained their excellent start to the new Premier League season, as they beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light, despite having to play much of the second half with ten men, after Pascal Struijk was shown a controversial red card.

item.title: Ipswich produce late fightback to stun winless Fulham
item.description: Two goals in three minutes sees Ipswich produce a late fightback to snatch a 2-1 victory against Fulham at Portman Road, with the away side still searching for their first Premier League win of the season.

item.title: Brentford extend unbeaten start as Ajer secures draw at Aston Villa
item.description: Brentford extend their unbeaten start to the new Premier League season as Kristoffer Ajer scores late to earn his side a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa, who's wait for a first home Premier League win of the season goes on.

item.title: Boos, anguish & fading belief -'worrying day' for under-pressure Carrick
item.description: It couldn't happen again could it? Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on Man Utd boss Michael Carrick after a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur.

item.title: 'I kissed Rodrigo and said thanks' - De Zerbi 'liked' Spurs red card
item.description: Roberto de Zerbi praises Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.

item.title: The rock behind Chelsea's entertainers: Midfield duo key for Blues
item.description: The performances of Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo underpinned Chelsea's 5-1 victory at home to Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Timely recognition or long overdue? How Gross is proving all-time bargain
item.description: Named the Premier League's player of the month for September, BBC Sport looks at Brighton star Pascal Gross' impact both this season and over the past nine years during his two spells at the club.

item.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portuguese FA
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month.

item.title: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue act
item.description: Heroics and battling performances have already become a theme of Arsenal's season with Bruno Guimaraes coming to the rescue again.

item.title: Arbeloa 'doesn't feel fear' but pressure increases after loss
item.description: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa says he does not 'feel fear' after defeat at Ipswich left his side winless in six games and bottom of the Premier League.

item.title: 'Reminds me of Muller' - Naderi proving worth in Rangers revival
item.description: After a slow start to his Rangers career, striker Ryan Naderi is playing an integral role in the club's title challenge and proving his doubters wrong.

item.title: AC Milan keen on Scott - Sunday's gossip
item.description: AC Milan are looking at Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Bayern Munich have held fresh talks with Manchester United's JJ Gabriel, Liverpool interested in Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, plus more.

item.title: I've got my own questions on Man City case - Carrick
item.description: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick says he was personally affected by the Manchester City case which has seen the club found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and still has questions about the matter.

item.title: Man City titles 'absolutely not' tainted - Maresca
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club's titles are "absolutely not" tainted after they were found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.

item.title: 'It hurts a lot' - Carrick 'understands' Man Utd boos after draw
item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says boos from the club's fans 'hurts a lot' but that he and his team 'must cope with it' after they conceded a late equaliser to draw 1-1 with Tottenham in the Premier League.

item.title: 'Tottenham needs this reaction' - De Zerbi defends Bentancur red
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi says the decision to send off Rodrigo Bentancur was correct, but admitted he liked that his player showed a 'reaction', adding he wants to see more of that attitude from his squad, following their 1-1 draw at Manchester United in the Premier League.

item.title: Bayern strike late to avoid shock defeat at Augsburg
